critical_code_review_comments: Fix on GamerTracksPage.js line 206 is correct and minimal: `key={`${t.track_id || 'x'}-${t.year ?? '_'}-${t.rank ?? i}`}` provides stable per-row identity even when the same track_id appears across multiple years (e.g. Smells Like Teen Spirit #2 in 1990 and #1 in 1991). React reconciliation now treats cross-year duplicates as distinct children without losing identity within a single render.

Backend seed retains the intentional cross-year duplicates (180 tracks contain 19 duplicate track_ids on hottest_100 first load) — this is by design and the fallback chain `track_id||'x'` + year + rank keeps the composite key unique.

rca of the issue: RCA: GamerTracksPage rendered Hottest 100 rows using `key={t.track_id || i}` while the seed assigns a hash-of-(title+artist) as track_id. A song appearing in multiple yearly Hottest 100 lists (e.g. Smells Like Teen Spirit #2/1990 and #1/1991) shares the SAME track_id, producing 19 duplicate React keys on first load (180-row unfiltered response). Fix at line 206 composes the key as `${track_id||'x'}-${year}-${rank}`, making cross-year duplicates render as distinct children. Verified: 180 rows still render, 0 duplicate-key warnings, year filter and search both work, no regressions on tab navigation.
